title: Anchor eval + cost model experiments
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working note for a small set of experiments that anchor cheaper-config proposals to a high-quality baseline, and a spreadsheet layout for recording results. The goal is to create deterministic quality gates (pass/fail) that tie into the Optimize product flow so we can automatically recommend cheaper configs only when risk is bounded. Unlike the prior "cost-of-quality" drafts, this focuses on an experiment-first calibration methodology and a tightly scoped spreadsheet schema we can share with SRE/Console for dashboards.

Definitions / scope
---
- Baseline (anchor): the high-cost, high-quality serving profile we use for reference (ex: gptx-16b fp16, no quant, batch=1).
- Cheaper config: any change intended to reduce per-token cost (quantization level, smaller model variant, reduced compute profile, enabled batching/caching).
- Eval set(s): production-like prompt slices and a holdout human-eval set. At minimum we require an overall set and 3 critical slices (auth flows, billing/legal, long-context summarization).
- Gate: a pass/fail rule expressed in metric deltas (absolute and relative) with slice-level constraints.

High-level acceptance criteria (proposal)
---
1) Overall quality gate: aggregated semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) or task-specific primary metric must not drop by more than 1.5 percentage points absolute versus anchor.
2) Critical-slice hard limits: for each critical slice, metric drop allowed <= 0.7 ppt absolute. Any slice exceeding this -> FAIL.
3) Hallucination guard: hallucination rate (as measured by our auto-checks + human spot-checks) must not exceed anchor + 0.3 ppt.
4) Latency/cost tradeoff: cost must improve by >= 15% and median token latency must remain within 1.25x of anchor (unless explicit SLO override).
5) Statistical significance: use bootstrap CI or paired t-test; require p < 0.05 for observed deltas if sample size > 200.

Spreadsheet schema (single-sheet canonical layout)
---
Column names (CSV style):
config_id, model_variant, quant_level, runtime_profile, batch_size, cache_enabled, anchor_flag, tokens_per_request_avg, avg_latency_ms, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, eval_set, primary_metric_mean, primary_metric_std, pct_delta_vs_anchor, slices_failed_count, slices_failed_list, hallucination_rate_pct, fuzzy_similarity_mean, pass_quality_gate, notes

Example row (text):
C-2026-001, gptx-16b-8bit, 8-bit, stock-runtime-v1, 8, true, false, 512, 42, 40, 95, 0.85, prod-overall, 0.912, 0.014, -0.011, 0, [], 0.42, 0.914, true, "quantized, ran with prefix cache, 24-hour run"

Anchoring mechanics (experiment plan)
---
1) Run anchor profile across eval set N=1000 requests per slice over 48 hours. Record metric mean + bootstrapped 95% CI.
2) Run candidate cheaper config(s) matched to same request IDs (paired measurement) to reduce noise.
3) Compute paired differences and bootstrap CI for delta; record pct_delta_vs_anchor.
4) If overall gate passes but any critical slice fails, mark config as "slice-failure" and do two additional investigations: (a) replicate with different random seed/batch placement, (b) human spot-check 50 examples from the failing slice.
5) For promising configs, do a 7-day shadow run on a small percentage of production traffic (canary) and monitor token-level cost and error traces.

Statistical guidance
---
- Prefer paired tests: compare metric(x_anchor) vs metric(x_candidate) on same prompt set.
- When N < 200 per slice, emphasize bootstrap CI over asymptotic p-values.
- Use Cohen's d for effect size reporting in addition to p-values.
- Record raw sample counts in spreadsheet; do not infer pass/fail without significance when delta is within 0.2 ppt.

Risk matrix / decision rules
---
- Fail-hard: Any candidate that increases hallucination > anchor + 0.5ppt, or any critical-slice drop > 1.5ppt -> do not promote.
- Fail-soft: If overall delta is between 1.5 and 2.5ppt but cost savings > 30%, escalate to product + compliance review and require extended human eval.
- Accept: Passes all gates and cost improvement >= 15% -> recommended for rollout with canary 5% traffic for 3 days.

Operational hooks to Console / Optimize
---
- Spreadsheet should export a single JSON line per config that the Console can ingest: key/value pairs matching column names.
- Add per-config alert thresholds in Console: if production monitoring later shows primary_metric drop > 0.5ppt vs experiment baseline for 1 hour -> automatic rollback.
- Expose tokens-per-candidate and token-cost breakdown for SLOs in the per-route dashboard.

Human evaluation protocol (short)
---
- When auto-metrics are within the soft band (0.7-1.5ppt overall delta), run blind human eval: 300 comparisons across slices, ordinal scoring 1-5 for correctness, and one explicit check for safety/hallucination.
- Use a consensus threshold (median >= 4) and note disagreement rate.

Outstanding questions / open experiments
---
- How sensitive are anchor deltas to batching differences? (we should run identical batch sizes and experimental placement to isolate quantization effect).
- Should we allow higher latency inflation for high-throughput routes where client perceptual latency isn't critical? (propose route-level SLO overrides).
- Automating slice selection: can we auto-derive critical slices from production error spikes? Need infra work (SRE ticket).

Next steps (immediate)
---
- Marco to prepare the canonical spreadsheet template and example dataset exports (ETA: 2026-02-27).
- Priya to run the first anchor baseline (dataset and sampling) and share results link (ETA: 2026-03-05).
- Evelyn to wire Console alert stub and a small ingestion schema for config JSON (ETA: 2026-03-07).

Appendix: small checklist for each candidate run
---
- [ ] Anchor baseline recorded (csv + timestamp)
- [ ] Candidate run matched to same request IDs (paired)
- [ ] Bootstrap CI computed and attached to spreadsheet
- [ ] Critical-slice per-slice metrics calculated
- [ ] Human-eval triggered if in soft band
- [ ] Console ingest JSON uploaded
- [ ] Canary rollout plan drafted (percent, duration, rollback triggers)

Notes on uniqueness vs prior docs
---
This doc intentionally frames the work as "anchored experiments" with a single canonical spreadsheet layout and explicit statistical rules for pass/fail. It is meant to sit upstream of the playbook and the more narrative cost-of-quality drafts: the output should be a machine-friendly CSV/JSON plus a short, deterministic gate that product/Console can operate on automatically.

End of note.
